\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:relative-lattice-action}
The action \eqref{eq:lattice-action} is free and properly discontinuous.  Its
quotient
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal J}_\Delta
   =(U^\circ\times\C^2\times\Delta)/\Lambda
\]
is a complex manifold, and the projection
\[
 \widetilde p:\widetilde{\mathcal J}_\Delta
   \longrightarrow U^\circ\times\Delta
\]
is a proper holomorphic submersion with fibres complex two-tori.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:relative-core}
The action \eqref{eq:Gamma-action} is free and properly discontinuous, and the
quotient
\[
 \mathcal J_\Delta
   =\widetilde{\mathcal J}_\Delta/\Gamma
\]
is a connected complex manifold.  For every $a\in\Delta$, the parameter
slice $(\operatorname{pr}_\Delta\circ p^\circ)^{-1}(a)$ is connected.  The
induced map
\[
 p^\circ:\mathcal J_\Delta\longrightarrow B^\circ\times\Delta
\]
is a proper holomorphic submersion, and each fibre over a point of
$B^\circ\times\{a\}$ is a complex two-torus with local period matrix
$\Omega_a$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:relative-finite-filling}
The quotient
\[
 \mathcal N_{j,\Delta}
   =\mathcal P_{j,\Delta}/\langle\widetilde g_j\rangle
\]
is a connected complex manifold, and every parameter slice of
$\mathcal N_{j,\Delta}\to\Delta$ is connected.  It has a proper holomorphic
map
\[
 F_j:\mathcal N_{j,\Delta}\longrightarrow D_j\times\Delta,
\]
and its projection to $\Delta$ is a holomorphic submersion.  The fibre over
$p_j\times\{a\}$ has multiplicity $m_j$, and its reduced structure is a
compact smooth complex surface.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:periodic-conical-fan}
The collection $\Sigma$ is a countable rational fan.  Every cone is generated
by part of a basis of $N'$.  For each vertex $v\in\Z^2$, the star fan of the
ray $\R_{\ge0}(v,1)$ is the finite complete hexagonal fan.  Consequently the
countable toric space
\[
 Y=Y_\Sigma
\]
is a smooth Hausdorff second-countable complex threefold, and the toric
divisor $E_v$ corresponding to the ray through $(v,1)$ is compact.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:relative-cusp}
The quotient
\[
 \mathcal N_{0,\Delta}
   =(Y_\varepsilon\times\Delta)/\Z^2
\]
is a connected Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold, and every
parameter slice of $\mathcal N_{0,\Delta}\to\Delta$ is connected.  The induced
map
\[
 F_0:\mathcal N_{0,\Delta}
     \longrightarrow D_\varepsilon\times\Delta
\]
is proper, and the projection to $\Delta$ is a holomorphic submersion.  The
inverse image
\[
 W_\Delta:=F_0^{-1}(\{0\}\times\Delta)
\]
is a reduced normal-crossing divisor in $\mathcal N_{0,\Delta}$.  For every
$a\in\Delta$, the fibre
\[
 W_a:=F_0^{-1}(0,a)
\]
is a compact, reduced, irreducible, nonnormal surface with normal-crossing
singularities, and its normalization is isomorphic to the compact toric
surface $E_0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:relative-compactification}
The map \eqref{eq:global-relative-map} is proper.  The parameter projection
\[
 \pi=\operatorname{pr}_\Delta\circ\mathfrak f:
 \mathfrak X_\Delta\longrightarrow\Delta
\]
is a proper holomorphic submersion.  Its fibre over $a$ is the compactification obtained from $\Omega_a$ by the
two logarithmic fillings and the cusp filling with the chosen valid cusp
cutoff.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:choice-independence}
The relative compactification has the following compatibility properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Fix a relatively compact parameter disc $\Delta\Subset\mathcal A$.
      If $0<\varepsilon'<\varepsilon$ are two valid cusp cutoffs
      for $\Delta$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:valid-cusp-cutoff}, then the two relative
      compactifications are canonically biholomorphic over $B\times\Delta$.
      The biholomorphism is the identity on the core and on the two finite
      fillings.
\item Let $\Delta_1,\Delta_2\Subset\mathcal A$ be parameter discs, with any valid cusp cutoffs in the sense of
      Definition~\ref{def:valid-cusp-cutoff} chosen in the two constructions.  Over
      $\Delta_1\cap\Delta_2$, their relative compactifications are
      canonically biholomorphic.  These identifications satisfy the cocycle
      identity on triple intersections.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, for every $a\in\mathcal A$, the fibre together with its
distinguished map to $B$ is independent, up to the canonical biholomorphisms
over $B$ constructed above, of the parameter disc and of the cusp cutoff.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:alpoge-member}
Let $(X^{\mathrm A},f^{\mathrm A})$ be the compact pair of
Alp\"oge~\cite[Construction~6.1]{AlpogeS6}, with its specified twists
$v_1=\widehat\gamma+2\widehat u-4\widehat w$ and
$v_2=-\widehat\gamma-3\widehat u+3\widehat w$, and untranslated cusp
gluing.
For its chosen admissible period function $\beta^{\mathrm A}$, there is a
unique constant $a_{\mathrm A}\in\mathcal A$ for which
$\beta^{\mathrm A}=\beta_0+a_{\mathrm A}$. For this parameter there is an
isomorphism of pairs
\[
 (X^{\mathrm A},f^{\mathrm A})\cong(X_{a_{\mathrm A}},f_{a_{\mathrm A}})
 \quad\text{over }B.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{nm:lem:unwrap}
For $m=3,4$ there is a connected regular unramified holomorphic covering
\[
 q_m:\mathcal Q_m\longrightarrow\mathcal M_m
\]
with deck group $\Z$, whose restriction to a smooth torus fibre is the
covering corresponding to the subgroup $\Lambda_0=\ker\gamma$ of the period
lattice.  For every $a_*\in\Delta$
there is a biholomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{nm:eq:product}
 \mathcal Q_m\simeq Q_{m,a_*}\times\Delta
\end{equation}
over $\C_b\times\Delta$, where $Q_{m,a_*}=\mathcal Q_m|_{a_*}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{nm:lem:actual-two-row-band}
For $m=3,4$, the cyclic covering $Q_{m,a_*}$ of
\cref{nm:lem:unwrap} has an analytic-Zariski open subset $Y_m$.
There is a smooth analytic surface $\mathcal E_m^{\rm an}$ proper over $\C_z$,
with precisely
the $m$ nodal fibres $z^m=1$, and a holomorphic line bundle
$L_m\to\mathcal E_m^{\rm an}$ for which $Y_m$ is a proper small
resolution of
\[
 H_m=\{A\otimes B=\Delta_m(z)\}
       \subset L_m\oplus L_m^{-1},
 \qquad
 \Delta_3=z^3-1,\quad \Delta_4=1-z^4.
\]
Its exceptional locus consists of one complete $\Pone$ over the
node of each nodal fibre.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:punctured-band}
Suppose $D\subset\mathcal K_m$ is a finite union of full $\Xi_m$-orbits and
$F\subset Y_m$ is finite. Then
\[
 Y_m\setminus(D\cup F)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 Y_{m,A}\setminus(D\cup F)
\]
are Oka.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:partial-exceptional}
Suppose $D,F$ satisfy the hypotheses of \cref{prop:punctured-band} and
$I\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}$. Then
\[
 Y_m\setminus\left(D\cup F\cup\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i\right)
\]
is Oka.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:local-conifold-curve}
For $R=\operatorname{Tot}(\cO_{\Pone}(-1)\oplus\cO_{\Pone}(-1))$ with zero
section $C\simeq\Pone$, one has
\[
 \operatorname{Bl}_C R\simeq
 \operatorname{Tot}(\cO_{\Pone\times\Pone}(-1,-1)),
\]
and this smooth algebraic threefold is algebraically elliptic and Oka.
\end{proposition}
